map.A two-variable adventure in five chapter: A story about two variables. It has five chapters and six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
Bad pattern in the harvest dome. Reader: you are on the crew. Get ready.
map.Previously: beneath city hall, the crew: Last time: under city hall, the crew opened Ada's balance vault. They cleared the inequality fog. The city can breathe again. But out at the farms, the glass dome drifts…
map.The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom Cit: The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom City. And it's dying. Idris, you and me. We lead this one.
map.Co-op mode accepted. Look — the mist is: Team mode on. Look. The mist is so thick. The crops can't find the sun.
map.Wilting rows, runaway mist, temperature: Dying rows. Mist out of control. The heat drifts all night. Each of you, grab a sensor.
Found it: the heat and air system. In there, causes and effects are mixed up.
map.Inside the dome. Fans the size of doors: Inside the dome. Fans as big as doors line the walls.
map.Test one. I run the fans; Owen reads the: Test one. I run the fans. Owen reads the heat. The longer the fans run, the cooler it gets.
map.Confirmed. Fan time up, temperature down: Yes. Fan time up, heat down. Each time we test.
map.Name your players. The independent varia: Name your players. You change the independent variable on purpose. It is the cause. The dependent variable answers it. It is the effect.
map.Two quantities, one relationship. Indepe: Two quantities. One relationship. Independent variable: the input. You control it. Dependent variable: the output. It depends on the input.
map.Game translation: independent is the but: In game words: independent is the button you press. Dependent is what happens on screen.
map.Your turn, reader. Tag the variables bef: Your turn, reader. Tag the variables. Then we touch the next dial.
map.Scenario from Sora's test: \"The longer: From Sora's test: "The longer the cooling fans run, the lower the dome temperature." Tag both variables. Pick one answer in EACH group.
map.Conceptual: the independent variable is: Conceptual: the independent variable is the cause. It is the thing you set on purpose. The dependent variable is the effect. It reacts. You can't set it yourself.
map.Procedural: try the plant test first: yo: Procedural: try the plant test first. You pick how much water to give. You set it, so it is independent. The plant's growth answers. It is dependent. Now read the fan sentence the same way. Which quantity gets SET? Which one REACTS?
map.VEX logged last night's temperature. A g: VEX logged the heat from last night. A graph is a picture of the relationship. Time goes across the bottom. Heat goes up the side.
map.Reading order: left to right. Like a sen: Read it left to right. Like a sentence.
map.This line falls steadily, then levels of: This line goes down at a steady rate. Then it is flat. Down means cooling. Flat means no change.
map.A graph shows how the dependent variable: A graph shows how the dependent variable changes. It is up the side. The independent variable goes across the bottom.
map.Match the graph to its story, reader. Th: Match the graph to its story, reader. The dome is talking. Listen with your eyes.
map.VEX projects last night's log: the line: VEX shows last night's log: the line falls steadily, then levels off flat. Which story does this graph tell? Tap the card that matches. Then CHECK.
map.Conceptual: a graph reads like a sentenc: Conceptual: read a graph like a sentence, left to right. Time goes on as you move right. The line's height is the heat at that time.
map.Procedural: split the line into its two: Procedural: cut the line into its two parts, in order. Part one slants down. What is the heat doing? Part two is flat. What is it doing now? Find the story with those two parts. Keep that order.
map.The irrigation deck. Pipes hum. A water: The water deck. Pipes hum. A water meter blinks numbers.
map.Water sensor data. A table puts the two: Water sensor data. A table puts the two variables side by side. Then the pattern can't hide.
map.Practice on a smaller machine first. A d: Try a small machine first. A drip line gave 1 hour → 3 liters, 2 → 6, 4 → 12. Its rule is the equation y = 3x. Each y is 3 times its x. See: the rule worked in EACH row.
map.An equation is a rule for computing the: An equation is a rule. It finds the dependent variable from the independent one. Test a rule on every row of the table. One lucky row proves nothing.
Now the main line. Hours in, liters out. Find its rule. Then we know how much water this dome needs.
Fill in the table. Then write the rule. Each row is a witness.
map.The main line's sensor log. Fill the mis: The main line's log. Fill in the missing value. Then pick the equation that matches every row.
map.Conceptual: the table hides one rule — e: Conceptual: the table hides one rule. Each y comes from its x the SAME way. It is so in each row. A rule that fits one row is luck. It is not a rule.
map.Procedural: compare each pair: 1 → 4, 2: Procedural: look at each pair: 1 → 4, 2 → 8, 3 → 12. Is y always the same MULTIPLE of its x? Find that multiplier with row one. Check it on rows two and three. Then use it at x = 5.
map.Same data, third costume. Plot hours and: Same data, new look. Plot hours and liters together. Each pair turns into a point. It is a coordinate pair (x, y).
map.Order is law: (hours, liters). Across fi: Order is the law: (hours, liters). Across first, then up. Flip them and you tell a new story.
map.The pump logged one reading before it cr: The pump logged one reading before it broke: "after 5 hours, 20 liters." That point is on this grid.
map.A coordinate pair (x, y) marks one momen: (x, y) is a coordinate pair. It marks one point of a relationship. x = the independent value. y = the dependent value. Order matters.
map.Tap the point that says it, reader — and: Tap the point that says it, reader. Only that point.
map.The pump's last reading: \"after 5 hours: The pump's last reading: "after 5 hours, 20 liters." Four points are on the grid. Tap the coordinate pair that means just that. Think of the order: (hours, liters).
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair reads (x, y): Conceptual: an ordered pair reads (x, y). Here that's (hours, liters). The first number tells how far ACROSS. The second number tells how far UP.
map.Procedural: walk along the hours axis to: Procedural: go along the hours axis. Stop at the hour in the log. Then go straight up to the liters. Tap the point where those two lines meet.
map.A hatch under the irrigation deck. Insid: A door under the water deck. Inside: the dome's first heat box. It is older than the glass.
map.Found our villain. No mastermind — just: Found our bad guy. Not a smart villain. Just a rusty heat box. Look at the wires.
map.It's been reading temperature as the INP: It used heat as the INPUT. It used fan time as the OUTPUT. It wired cause and effect the wrong way.
map.Confirmed. It swapped the independent an: Yes. It swapped the independent and dependent variables. For years the dome bossed the heat. It obeyed the fans. Sad. Almost like a poem.
map.Final quest chain: reseed the wilted row: Last quest: plant seeds in the dead rows. We fix the wires. The seed drone drops 9 pods each minute it flies. Rule: d = 9t.
map.The drone's equation: d = 9t, where t =: The drone's equation: d = 9t. t = minutes flying (independent). d = seed pods dropped (dependent).
map.Fly the drone by the rule, reader. The w: Fly the drone by the rule, reader. The dead rows need you.
map.The seed drone obeys d = 9t (t = minutes: The seed drone uses d = 9t. t = minutes flying → d = seed pods dropped. Run the rule both ways. Plant the dead rows.

map.Procedural: forward — substitute the t-v: Procedural: forward: substitute the t-value. Multiply by 9. Backward: ask this. 9 times WHAT minutes gives that many pods? Division undoes the multiplication.
map.The controller hatch, 4:51 AM. Sunrise i: The heat box door, 4:51 AM. The sun comes up in nine minutes. Three wire locks left.
map.Three locks stand between this dome and: Three locks stand between this dome and the sun. Each one is a relationship. The heat box must learn it again.
map.Temperature recovery, the water budget,: The heat coming back. The water plan. And one last wire question. Reader, hands on.
map.Cross these wires right, and the dome wa: Cross these wires right. Then the dome wakes up with the sun.
map.Boss Gate: substitute, compute, compare: Boss Gate: substitute, work it out, compare. And show you know which variable depends on which.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The controller i: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The heat box is listening. Teach it well.
map.Sunrise is coming. Three wire locks — ea: The sun is coming. Three wire locks. Each is a relationship. The heat box must learn it again. Substitute, work it out, compare… Tag the variables right.

map.Conceptual: every lock is one rule relat: Conceptual: each lock is one rule with two variables. Substitute the value you KNOW. The rule finds the one you don't. And think of the heat box's old mistake. Be sure which variable is the answer.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — replace x with the: Procedural: Lock 1: put the hours in for x. Then add. Lock 2: multiply the hours by 6. Then compare it with the 60 liters the tank holds. Lock 3: the independent variable is the INPUT. It is the quantity you choose. The rule finds the other one from it.
map.Rows up! Mist clearing! Temperature righ: Rows up! Mist going away! The heat is just what the rule said.
map.The controller finally asks the right qu: The heat box asks the right question at last: what depends on what.
map.Achievement unlocked: harvest saved. Rol: Level won: harvest saved. The end?
map.…Crew. The Pattern Engine is waking bene: …Crew. The Pattern Engine is waking up under the city. Each part of town is glowing. Five shapes stand over its heart. Four of us. And you. Not a bad pattern. A start.
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew boss. Keeps the notebook. Asks the next question. In this volume: co-led the dome rescue. Called the last wire fix.
map.Evidence officer. Tests every rule on ev: Proof finder. Tests each rule on each row. In this volume: read the table that showed the dome's water rule.
map.Builder and fixer. Keeps the sensors hon: Builder and fixer. Keeps the sensors true. In this volume: fixed a heat box older than she is.
Pattern finder. Co-led the dome rescue. In this volume: flew the seed drone by its own equation.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. It can sense bad patterns. It can't do math. That's your job.
map.Independent variable.The quantity you ch: Independent variable.The quantity you change on purpose. The cause. How long the fans run.
map.Dependent variable.The quantity that res: Dependent variable.The quantity that reacts. The effect. How hot the dome is.
map.Graph.A picture of the relationship. Rea: Graph.A picture of the relationship. Read left to right. Line goes down = getting less. Flat line = staying the same.
map.Table & equation.A table lists matching: Table & equation.A table lists x–y pairs that match. An equation like y = 4x is the rule. A true rule works in each row.

map.Burn time is the quantity being allowed: Burn time is the quantity that changes on purpose. It is the independent variable (the cause).
map.The candle's height responds to that tim: The candle's height reacts to that time. It is the dependent variable (the effect).

map.A different graph: a line that climbs st: A new graph: a line that goes up at a steady rate. Then it goes flat.
map.Climbing piece = the quantity is increas: The part that goes up = the quantity gets bigger. Like a tub filling.
map.Flat piece = no change — the tap is off;: The flat part = no change. The tap is off. The water stays put. Story: "it goes up, then stays put."
map.On a graph, a line that stays flat the w: A flat graph shows a quantity that is… (write: changing or constant)

map.Using the rule y = 3x, what is y when x: Use the rule y = 3x. What is y when x = 7?
map.Different pump, rule y = 2x: the reading: A new pump. Rule y = 2x. The reading "after 3 hours, 6 liters" is the pair (3, 6).
map.Across to 3 on the hours axis, up to 6 o: Go across to 3 on the hours axis. Go up to 6 on the liters axis. That's the point.

map.A practice controller: temperature rule: A test heat box: heat rule y = x + 8. At x = 30 hours, y = 30 + 8 = 38 degrees.
map.Its water rule m = 4t: at t = 7, m = 4 ×: Its water rule is m = 4t. At t = 7, m = 4 × 7 = 28 liters. The tank holds 30 → 28 ≤ 30, so it fits.
map.In m = 4t, t is the value you choose and: In m = 4t, you choose t. m is found FROM it. So t is the independent variable. m is the dependent one.
map.With the rule y = x + 8, what is y when: Use the rule y = x + 8. What is y when x = 50?
map.Pick one tag in EACH group — a cause and: Pick one tag in EACH group. A cause and an effect.
map.Fan time is the cause you control; the t: Fan time is the cause you control. The heat answers it. Tagged and logged!
map.Swapped! That's the old controller's exa: Swapped! That's the old heat box's mistake. The heat does not make the fans run.
map.The fans' color never changes and change: The fans' color never changes. It changes nothing. It is not a variable in this story.
map.The crops care about the result, but the: The crops care about the result. But they are not one of the two quantities. They don't change here.
map.One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do w: One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do we SET? Which one REACTS?
map.Falling line, then flat line — cooling,: Line goes down, then flat. Cooling, then the same. You read the dome's story well.
map.Read left to right, like a sentence — on: Read left to right, like a sentence. On this graph the FALL comes first. Then the flat part.
map.Rising first would slant UP at the start: Going up first would slant UP at the start. But this line starts by going down. It never goes back up.
map.Falling then rising would make a V shape: Down then up would make a V shape. After the fall, this line stays flat.
map.Careful — y = x + 3 works for (1, 4) onl: Look again. y = x + 3 works for (1, 4) only. Test EACH row. Is 2 + 3 = 8? Keep the rule that works for all four.

map.Cell's right — now pick the equation tha: The cell is right. Now pick the equation that matches each row.
